# Midland Development Corporation, Midland International Air & Space Port, Spaceport America, and Starfighters Space Sign Letter of Intent to Develop a High-Speed Flight Test and Space Launch Corridor


November 18, 2026 9:00am EST


*Four-party letter of intent targets a dedicated corridor spanning over 250 miles between two FAA-licensed spaceports for supersonic and hypersonic flight testing, regulatory development, and space launch and reentry operations*


MIDLAND, Texas--(BUSINESS WIRE)--[Midland Development Corporation](https://www.midlandtxedc.com/) (“MDC”),[Midland International Air & Space Port](https://www.flymaf.com/) (“MAF”), the[New Mexico Spaceport Authority](https://www.spaceportamerica.com/) (“NMSA”), operator of Spaceport America, and[Starfighters Space, Inc.](https://starfightersspace.com/) ("Starfighters”) (NYSE American: FJET), have signed a letter of intent (“LOI”) to jointly define, advocate for, and develop a dedicated high-speed flight test corridor and inland space launch range between the two FAA-licensed spaceports.


The proposed corridor would span approximately 250 nautical miles of sparsely populated West Texas and southern New Mexico airspace between Midland International Air & Space Port and Spaceport America. The parties intend that the proposed corridor support repeatable, high-cadence supersonic and hypersonic flight testing, including sonic boom overpressure measurement and air traffic integration procedure development. A long-term goal of the corridor is to one day support operations to and above the Kármán line for suborbital and orbital launch, air launch, point-to-point spaceflight, and the reentry and recovery of spaceflight vehicles and payloads.


The LOI follows two federal actions now before the FAA. A rulemaking under Docket No. FAA-2026-6935, implementing Executive Order 14304, Leading the World in Supersonic Flight, would replace the longstanding prohibition on overland flight above Mach 1 with a measurable ground-level overpressure standard. A separate request for information under Docket No. FAA-2026-9736, implementing Executive Order 14369, Ensuring American Space Superiority, seeks public input on designating priority airspace for launch and reentry operations and on expanding U.S. spaceport capacity. The parties believe a single, well-placed corridor serving multiple licensed spaceports can serve both FAA purposes, while also supporting the national interest in inland launch capacity and national security requirements for hypersonic technology development.


The LOI precedes a memorandum of understanding (“MOU”) that the parties plan to develop jointly to define their respective roles and interests in the corridor’s development.


“This partnership builds on Midland’s growing role in the commercial space and aerospace industries,” said Brad Bullock, Executive Director, Midland Development Corporation. “A dedicated high-speed flight test and space launch corridor will strengthen the capabilities of Midland International Air & Space Port, create new opportunities for aerospace and defense companies to conduct research, testing, and development here, and make Midland a more competitive location for businesses considering where to establish or expand their operations. We are proud to support this collaboration and its potential to attract new investment, high-skilled jobs, and long-term economic activity to Midland.”


“When Midland International Air & Space Port became the first commercial service airport in the nation to receive a spaceport license in 2014, we recognized the tremendous potential of bringing aviation and space together,” said Justine Ruff, Director the Midland International Air & Space Port. “This collaboration represents the next step in realizing that vision. By connecting two licensed spaceports through a dedicated high-speed flight corridor, we have an opportunity to help shape the future of aerospace while demonstrating how traditional aviation and emerging space technologies can safely and successfully coexist.”


“The possibility of an inland high-speed flight corridor between Spaceport America in New Mexico, and Midland International Air & Space Port in Texas, is very exciting, and would uniquely enable subsonic and supersonic tests and high-altitude experiments,” said Scott McLaughlin, Executive Director of Spaceport America. “We look forward to working to implementing this to serve both national security and civil needs, and to build the aerospace ecosystem in both locations.”


“Federal policy is moving faster than the infrastructure, and the country needs a place to fly these vehicles and prove out the procedures that go with them,” said Tim Franta, CEO of Starfighters Space. “A corridor anchored by two licensed spaceports, over some of the least populated airspace in the country, is the most practical answer we have seen. Starfighters intends to fly it first and give the FAA real data to work from.”


Spaceport America and the Midland International Air & Space Port each hold an FAA Launch Site Operator License. Starfighters operates its supersonic F-104 aircraft at Midland International Air & Space Port, with a flight range that encompasses both spaceports. Starfighters is also developing an air-launch system that could ultimately use the corridor for suborbital and orbital launch operations.


The LOI is an expression of the parties’ mutual intent. It does not obligate or transfer funds among the parties, and any exchange of funds, services, or facility access would be the subject of separate written agreements.


**About Midland Development Corporation**


[Midland Development Corporation](https://www.midlandtxedc.com/) (MDC) was created in January 2002 to promote business expansion, job creation, and capital investment to diversify and strengthen the Midland, Texas, economy. The MDC does so by offering incentives to qualified new and existing employers that create jobs for the community. Midland voters made these incentives possible when they approved a quarter-cent increase in the local sales tax rate, with additional revenues earmarked to promote economic development and diversification.


**About Midland International Air & Space Port**


[Midland International Air & Space Port](https://www.flymaf.com/) (MAF) is owned and operated by the City of Midland, Texas, and provides scheduled airline service for Midland, Odessa, and the surrounding Permian Basin. In 2014, MAF became the first primary commercial service airport in the United States to receive an FAA Launch Site Operator License, making it the first commercial spaceport co-located with an FAA Part 139 commercial airport. The spaceport supports horizontal launch operations and aerospace research, development, and flight testing.


**About the New Mexico Spaceport Authority and Spaceport America**


The[New Mexico Spaceport Authority](https://www.spaceportamerica.com/) (NMSA) is the State of New Mexico agency that operates Spaceport America, the world’s first purpose-built commercial spaceport. The FAA-licensed horizontal and vertical launch site covers 18,000 acres in southern New Mexico beside the U.S. Army’s White Sands Missile Range, with access to 6,000 square miles of restricted airspace, a 12,000-foot runway, and vertical launch complexes. Tenants include Virgin Galactic, Hermeus, UP Aerospace, and SpinLaunch.


**About Starfighters Space, Inc.**


[Starfighters Space](https://starfightersspace.com/) (NYSE American: FJET), with a fleet of F-104 aircraft based at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida and the Midland International Air and Space Port in Texas, is the only company in the world with the commercial capability to fly at sustained Mach 2+ speeds for a variety of aerospace applications. The iconic F-104 jets are configurable as a platform for air-launched payloads, training for pilots, and to support research, development, test, and evaluation (RDT&E) for hypersonic technologies, advanced materials, missile defense systems, microgravity science, spaceflight hardware validation, and defense electronic systems.
